title: Staged traffic shepherding for stream-consistent multi-region failover
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement: Hosted API gateways currently perform coarse-grained failover which causes streaming connections and long-lived sessions to drop or to incur complete KV cache misses after failover, creating user-visible regressions and SLO breaches. We need a multi-region failover approach that preserves streaming session continuity where possible, avoids mass reconnect storms, and enforces graceful degradation (load shedding + circuit breakers) when regions breach SLAs or resource exhaustion occurs.

Goal: Implement a staged traffic shepherding system at the edge gateway that performs incremental traffic shifts with session/stream awareness, streaming drain logic, and congestion-aware circuit breakers so that: (1) p95/p99 client-observed streaming disconnects do not regress during failover, (2) error-budget-driven load-shedding triggers avoid cascading failures, and (3) operators can run a safe canary and rollback from the Console with clear telemetry and automated safety gates.
acceptance_criteria: Gate 1: Canary shift of 5% production traffic to target region while preserving existing long-lived streams (no client-visible disconnects above baseline + 0.2 percentage points).
Gate 2: When a region is marked degraded, active streaming connections are drained with graceful resume tokens; <2% of resumed streams see protocol-level errors within 60s of reconnection.
Gate 3: Circuit breakers at gateway and per-backend enforce backoff when p95 latency > target SLO for 2 consecutive minutes and reduce accepted concurrency by configurable steps (default 25%).
Gate 4: Load-shedding policy automatically returns 429 with structured JSON and retry-after header for non-critical routes, preserving critical routes (auth, billing) unless operator overrides.
Gate 5: Console widgets show region health, error-budget burn rate, streaming reconnect-rate, and the active shepherding plan; operators can pause or rollback shifts with a single click.
Gate 6: Conflict tests: synthetic sessions injection during canary exercises must not cause a >10% increase in prefix-KV-miss rate in healthy region.
Gate 7: All new code covered by unit & integration tests; e2e soak test for 24h with induced partial outage reproduces rollback path and metrics behave as expected.
engineering_notes: Overall approach: implement 'staged shepherd' controller in gateway control-plane that orchestrates traffic weight adjustments in small increments (default 5%) while coordinating per-connection drain/resume tokens with the serving runtime.

Session model: introduce ephemeral connection token (ECT) at handshake that allows the runtime to map a resumed HTTP/2 or WebSocket stream to a prior KV cache fingerprint. If resume fails, fallback policy routes to nearest compatible model variant to avoid high latency cold-starts.

Circuit-breaker model: two-layer breakers. (1) Region-level breaker driven by aggregated SLO signals (p95 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU queue depth). (2) Route-level breaker using per-route concurrency and recent 5m error trend. Both should be configurable via Console and expose reason codes for observability.

Backpressure & load-shedding: implement token bucket admission at edge with hierarchy: critical routes > standard routes > best-effort routes. Best-effort routes get probabilistic early 429s under overload with structured guidance for clients to backoff. Use randomized jitter on retry-after to avoid thundering herds.

KV cache preservation: add 'prefix-aware routing' header so requests containing a cacheable prefix can be steered to nodes with warm KV state during an incremental migration window. The shepherd controller tracks prefix hit-rate and slows traffic movement when warm-hit < threshold.

Streaming drain: upon decision to move connections, controller signals edge to mark connection for 'soft drain' — new inbound requests are rerouted, in-flight tokens are offered resume tokens, and client-facing API returns a structured 'resume-capable' close event. We will reuse existing function-calling framing to encode resume metadata.

Observability: emit new metrics: shepherd_shift_progress{plan_id,from_region,to_region}, streaming_resume_success_rate, stream_reconnect_latency_ms_p95, region_error_budget_burn_rate, gateway_breaker_state, prefix_kv_hit_rate. Create Grafana dashboards and SLO alerts tied to error budget burn windows.

Compatibility: ensure staged shepherding is backward-compatible with older SDKs by falling back to pure per-request routing when ECT header missing. Make the feature opt-in per customer via tenant config in control-plane.
rollout_plan: Dev: unit tests + integration tests against local runtime shim; feature flag gating and developer docs (1 week).
Internal canary: 1% internal API traffic across us-west1->us-east1 with synthetic stream injection (48h soak). Monitor streaming_reconnect_rate and prefix_kv_hit_rate. (3 days).
Customer beta: opt-in list of 3 low-risk customers, 5% traffic with operator-run shepherd plan; collect feedback and incidents (2 weeks).
Gradual production rollout: incremental 5% steps with 1h observation windows and auto-rollback on guardrails (error-budget-burn > 3x baseline or streaming reconnect spikes).
Full launch: enable Console controls, runbook, and postmortem template; include safety toggles for emergency drain or force-redispatch.
